'''Professional Football Club Ludogorets 1945''' ({{langx|bg|Професионален Футболен Клуб „Лудогорец 1945“|Profesionalen Futbolen Klub Ludogorets 1945}}), commonly known as '''Ludogorets Razgrad''', '''Ludogorets 1945''' or simply '''Ludogorets''', is a Bulgarian professional association football club based in [[Razgrad]], which currently competes in the [[First Professional Football League (Bulgaria)|First Professional Football League]], the top tier of the Bulgarian football league system.

In their [[2011–12 A Group|inaugural 2011–12 season]] in A Group after promotion, Ludogorets made headlines by capturing the league championship and the [[Bulgarian Cup]]. Subsequently, the club made a significant continental impact in the [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League]] when they reached the [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League#Round of 16|Round of 16]] in only their second European run. To date they have reached the knockout stages of the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] four times, more than any other club in Bulgaria. Ludogorets are also only the second Bulgarian team after [[PFC Levski Sofia|Levski Sofia]] to enter the main phase of the [[UEFA Champions League]], a feat which they achieved in the following 2014–15 season. During that same campaign they became the first Bulgarian team to score points in the modern Champions League following a 1–0 win over [[FC Basel|Basel]] in [[Sofia]].

Since their promotion to the Bulgarian top-flight in 2011, Ludogorets have established themselves as a dominant force in Bulgarian football, winning 14 consecutive titles.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ludogorets.com/en/news/?i=2043|title=Ludogorets won the sixth title with a record breaking score!|website=www.ludogorets.com|access-date=18 June 2019|archive-date=18 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190618105642/https://www.ludogorets.com/en/news/?i=2043|url-status=live}}</ref> They have also won the Bulgarian Cup four times, as well as the Bulgarian Supercup on nine occasions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ludogorets.com/en/hall-of-fame/european-tournaments/|title=Achievements, records & performance – PFC Ludogorets|website=www.ludogorets.com|access-date=18 June 2019|archive-date=18 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190618105632/https://www.ludogorets.com/en/hall-of-fame/european-tournaments/|url-status=live}}</ref> The latter is a record in Bulgarian football.

Ludogorets' traditional home colours are green and white. The club's home ground is the [[Huvepharma Arena]] in Razgrad, a stadium with a capacity of 10,423 spectators.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://football.sportal.bg/news.php?news=363917|title="Лудогорец Арена" с най-модерното осветление|website=sportal.bg|access-date=3 May 2017|archive-date=30 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170830012224/https://football.sportal.bg/news.php?news=363917|url-status=live}}</ref>"}}
